findings.title: The new downsize definition replaces the existing width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature: this second `self.downsize` definition replaces the definition accepting `max_width, max_height, opts`. Existing callers passing width and height now either raise ArgumentError (when also passing options) or pass the height as `opts`, causing `optimize` to fail when it accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve a single method that supports both calling conventions, or give the dimensions-string variant a different name.

findings.title: Large animated GIF uploads lose their animation even when allowed
findings.body: The resize call passes the temporary file's path rather than a path with the original filename's extension. `OptimizedImage.optimize` only selects its animated implementation when the source path ends in `.gif`, but multipart upload temporary paths normally have no such extension. Consequently, even with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, a large animated GIF goes through the `convert` instructions using `[0]` and is permanently replaced by its first frame. Detect animation/image type independently of the temporary path before modifying the original upload.

findings.title: The fixed size limit also overrides attachment upload settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` validates both images and attachments, but the new unconditional 10 MB limit replaces `max_attachment_size_kb` as well as the image limit. Attachments cannot benefit from the new image downsizing: sites permitting attachments larger than 10 MB now have valid uploads blocked in the browser, while sites with smaller attachment limits unnecessarily accept files for upload that the server will reject. Apply the relaxed limit only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.
